{{Short description|Geometric theorem}}
In [[geometry]], '''Hesse's principle of transfer''' ({{langx|de|Übertragungsprinzip}}) states that if the points of the [[projective line]] '''P'''<sup>1</sup> are depicted by a [[rational normal curve]] in '''P'''<sup>''n''</sup>, then the [[Group (mathematics)|group]] of the [[projective transformation]]s of '''P'''<sup>''n''</sup> that preserve the curve is [[isomorphic]] to the group of the projective transformations of '''P'''<sup>1</sup> (this is a generalization of the original Hesse's principle, in a form suggested by [[Wilhelm Franz Meyer]]).<ref name="Meyer">{{cite book|author=W.F. Meyer|author-link=Wilhelm Franz Meyer|title=Apolaritat Und Rationale Curven|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=t-wOAwAAQBAJ|isbn=978-5-87713-744-8}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_8eaAwAAQBAJ&pg=PA102|title=Élie Cartan (1869–1951)|last=Akivis|first=M. A.|last2=Rosenfeld|first2=B. A.|year=2011|publisher=American Mathematical Soc.|isbn=9780821853559|language=en|pages=102, 107–108}}</ref> It was originally introduced by [[Otto Hesse]] in 1866, in a more restricted form. It influenced [[Felix Klein]] in the development of the [[Erlangen program]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XTYDCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA111|title=Mathematics of the 19th Century: Geometry, Analytic Function Theory|editor-last=[[Kolmogorov]]|editor-first=Andrei N.|editor-last2=Yushkevich|editor-first2=Adolf-Andrei P.|year=2012|publisher=Birkhäuser|isbn=9783034891738|language=en|page=111}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bvy0aANuhPYC&pg=PA25|title=From a Geometrical Point of View: A Study of the History and Philosophy of Category Theory|last=Marquis|first=Jean-Pierre|year=2008|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=9781402093845|language=en|page=25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=F_NP8Kub2XYC&pg=PA179|title=Perspectives on Projective Geometry: A Guided Tour Through Real and Complex Geometry|last=Richter-Gebert|first=Jürgen|year=2011|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=9783642172861|language=en|page=179}}</ref> Since its original conception, it was generalized by many mathematicians, including [[Felix Klein|Klein]], [[Gino Fano|Fano]], and [[Élie Cartan|Cartan]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/emergenceoftheor0000hawk|url-access=registration|title=Emergence of the Theory of Lie Groups: An Essay in the History of Mathematics 1869–1926|last=Hawkins|first=Thomas|year=2000|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=9780387989631|language=en|pages=[https://archive.org/details/emergenceoftheor0000hawk/page/234 234] and 294}}</ref>
